{{Short description|Numeral system from the Glagolitic script}}
[[File:Vinodol.jpg|thumb|The first line of the [[Law code of Vinodol|Vinodol statute]] includes the year 1280 written as {{Script/Glagolitic|·Ⱍ҃·Ⱄ҃·Ⱁ҃·}} (16th century copy of the statute).]]
{{Table_Numeral_Systems}}
{{Contains special characters|Glagolitic}}

'''Glagolitic numerals''' are a [[numeral system]] derived from the [[Glagolitic script]], generally agreed to have been created in the 9th century by [[Saints Cyril and Methodius|Saint Cyril]]. They are similar to [[Cyrillic numerals]], except that numeric values are assigned according to the native [[alphabetic order]] of the [[Glagolitic alphabet]].<ref name="Schenker1995">{{Citation| last=Schenker| first=Alexander M. |author-link=Alexander M. Schenker |title=The Dawn of Slavic: An Introduction to Slavic Philology |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=0lzGQgAACAAJ |publisher=Yale University Press |location=New Haven, Connecticut |year=1995 |isbn=0-300-05846-2}}</ref><ref name="Lunt2001">{{cite book|last=Lunt|first=Horace Gray |author-link=Horace Lunt |title=Old Church Slavonic Grammar|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=7BXJgfIo_fYC&pg=PA16|edition=7th|year=2001|publisher=Walter de Gruyter|location=Berlin, Germany|isbn=978-3-11-016284-4|pages=16–18}}</ref> Use of Glagolitic script and numerals declined through the Middle Ages and by the 17th century Glagolitic was used almost only in religious writings. It is unclear if the use of Glagolitic numerals persisted as long as the use of Glagolitic script.<ref name="Chrisomalis2010">{{cite book|last=Chrisomalis|first=Stephen|title=Numerical Notation: A Comparative History|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=kXZhBAAAQBAJ&pg=PA178|access-date=2016-12-28|year=2010|publisher=Cambridge University Press|location=Cambridge, England|isbn=978-1-139-48533-3|pages=178–182}}</ref>

==General description==
The system is a decimal [[alphabetic numeral system]], with values assigned in alphabetical order, so {{Script/Glagolitic|Ⰰ}} {{IPAblink|ɑ}} = 1, {{Script/Glagolitic|Ⰱ}} {{IPAblink|b}} = 2, and so forth. Glyphs for the ones, tens, and hundreds values are combined additively to form numbers, for example, {{Script/Glagolitic|ⰗⰑⰂ}} is 500 + 80 + 3 or 583. Numbers are written from left to right, highest value at the left. As with Cyrillic numerals, between 11 and 19 the ordinary sign order is reversed, so the numbers 11 through 19 are typically written with the ones digit before the glyph for 10; for example {{Script/Glagolitic|ⰅⰊ}} is 6 + 10, making 16, this reflects the Slavic lexical numerals for the teens.<ref name="KentLancour1979">{{cite book|editor1=A. Kent|editor2=H. Lancour|editor3=J.E. Daily|editor4=W.Z. Nasri|title=Encyclopedia of Library and Information Science|chapter-url=https://books.google.com/books?id=jU3fwyjqS5UC&pg=PA513|access-date=26 March 2018|volume=27|date=1979|publisher=Marcel Dekker Inc.|location=New York, NY|isbn=978-0-8247-2027-8|pages=510–520|chapter=Slavic Paleography}}</ref><ref name="Chrisomalis2010" />

For numbers greater than 999, there is conflicting evidence. As the earliest version of the Glagolitic alphabet had 36 characters, there are indications of the use of Glagolitic letters for 1000 through 9000,<ref name="Chrisomalis2010" /><ref>{{cite conference |last=Veder |first=William R. |title=The Glagolitic Alphabet as a Text |url=https://www.academia.edu/8615898 |conference=Glagoljica i hrvatski glagolizam. Zbornik radova s međunarodnoga znanstvenog skupa povodom 100. obljetnice Staroslavenske akademije i 50. obljetnice Staroslavenskog instituta |publisher=Staroslavenski Institut/Krčka Biskupija |place=Zagreb, Croatia |year=2004 |pages=375–387 }}</ref> although the validity of 3000 and greater is questioned.<ref name="Mathiesen">{{cite thesis |last=Mathiesen |first=Robert |date=2004 |title=A New Reconstruction of the Original Glagolitic Alphabet  |type=M.S. |publisher=Brown University |url=https://www.academia.edu/7784124 }}</ref> There is also evidence of the use of a thousands sign, similar to the [[wikt:͵|lower-left keraia]] in [[Greek numerals]] or the [[wikt:҂|Cyrillic thousands sign]] to mark numbers greater than 999.<ref name="Chrisomalis2010" />

To distinguish numbers from text, numerals are typically set apart with dots or a mark is placed over the numbers.<ref name="Chrisomalis2010" /> For example, the ''[[Missale Romanum Glagolitice]]'' printed in 1483, uses both dots around and a [[titlo]] over letters in places to indicate a number,<ref>{{cite web|title=Hrvatski glagoljički Prvotisak misala iz 1483|trans-title=Croatian Glagolitic First Printing of the 1483 Missal|language=hr|date=2013|first=Darko|last=Žubrinić|url=http://www.croatianhistory.net/etf/1483.html|access-date=22 May 2020}}</ref> as does the [[Law code of Vinodol|Vinodol statute]].

Example: [[File:Glagolitic numerals-1280.svg|45px|class=skin-invert]] ({{Script/Glagolitic|·Ⱍ҃·Ⱄ҃·Ⱁ҃·}}) – 1280

As noted earlier, the letters associated with number values greater than 999 are uncertain, and different authors have inferred different values (and different orders) for letters towards the end of the Glagolitic alphabet.<ref name="Mathiesen" /><ref>{{cite web|title=Glagoling the Glagolithic ("Speaking the Speakolithic")|last=Chulev|first=Basil|date=2015|url=https://www.academia.edu/17371522|access-date=May 21, 2020}}</ref>
